messages:
alex_support: FYI acme reported 400s from /embeddings. Error: \"Invalid embedding length: expected 1536, got 1\". They say it started after a client update. Pasting their curl and error below.

alex_support: ```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "input": "their single string here"
}

Response 400: {"error":{"message":"Invalid embedding length: expected 1536, got 1"}}
```

matt_engineer: Hmm that looks like the client sent a single string (scalar) instead of an array. Our embeddings expect either \"input\": ["...", ...] or for the SDK we accept singletons but the HTTP proto requires arrays. Is there any middleware that might stringify arrays?

jenni_qa: Quick note: I've seen axios users accidentally set `transformRequest` that does `JSON.stringify(Object.values(payload))` which turns `input: ["a"]` -> `"[\"a\"]"`. That would explain length 1. Can we ask for raw request body (not just curl)?

alex_support: Customer pasted the raw body from their webapp (they use a custom wrapper). They confirmed they call `JSON.stringify(reqBody)` twice in one codepath.

matt_engineer: ok repro steps to share with them — two variants.

matt_engineer: Incorrect (what we saw):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json

{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"[\"single sentence\"]"}
```

matt_engineer: Correct: top-level input must be an array (not a string)
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json

{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":["single sentence"]}
```

jenni_qa: Also check Content-Type. If they try NDJSON or gzip headers but send JSON string it can confuse proxies. Example header mistakes: `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson` but body is full JSON string.

opsbot: deploy-log:embedding-service: warning: received malformed input from client  acct/acme - rejected request id=rc_01Fxxxxx

sre_liz: For remediation recommended steps: 1) ask them to log `typeof body` and `body.input instanceof Array` on client before send. 2) Send them a tiny node snippet to validate: 
```js
// validateInput.js
const payload = { model: 'text-embedding-3-small', input: 'hello' };
console.log(typeof payload.input); // -> string
console.log(Array.isArray(payload.input)); // -> false
// convert
payload.input = Array.isArray(payload.input) ? payload.input : [payload.input];
```

alex_support: I shared that snippet with customer and asked for headers + raw bytes. They replied they were double-JSON-stringifying because of an old middleware that persisted requests to a queue.

jenni_qa: Good catch. Also flagged that our docs examples show both single and batch shapes — maybe ambiguous. We should add a clear example of the raw HTTP body for a singleton vs batch and how SDKs map to it. Filing follow-up ticket.

matt_engineer: Workaround for now: accept the stringified array by parsing if `typeof input === 'string' && input.startsWith('[')` — but only in downstream debugging layer, not as long-term fix. I'll add a temporary guard in the proxy to return a clearer 400: "malformed input: embedding input must be array of strings, not JSON-encoded string".

sre_liz: Can you add logging that prints `typeof input` and length of parsed array (if any)? Want to track how many requests hit this.

matt_engineer: Yep will add telemetry. Also added a short unit test to ensure `"input": "[\"a\"]"` is rejected with our clearer message.

alex_support: Customer applied fix on their side and confirmed embeddings working again. They also asked for a note in onboarding docs about queue persistence causing double-stringify.

jenni_qa: I'll update the docs and add an example of the queue case + recommended validation before enqueue.

alex_support: Thanks all. Closing ticket after docs patch and the proxy guard is live. :white_check_mark:
